summary: John's 2nd great-grandfather; born in Baden in 1866, brought to Pennsylvania as a toddler in 1868; an iron moulder for nearly 50 years in Hazleton, Tamaqua and Wilkes-Barre.
bio: Henry J. Meier was born 15 Nov 1866 in Germany (Baden), the fourth child and second son of Friedrich Mayer, mason, and Maria Anna Birkenmaier of Munzingen near Freiburg. His German birth/baptism record has not been located (he was born after his parents' 1862 Munzingen marriage; the Munzingen 1866 birth register L 10 Nr. 1591 should hold it — not yet read). By his own account in the 1910 census he immigrated in 1868; the family crossed together (Friedrich, Maria and four small children) between Nov 1866 and Sept 1869; ship and port not found. He appears as 'Henry, 4, Baden' in the 1870 census (Hazleton East Ward, 8 Jun 1870, 'Meyer' household) and 'Henry, 14, son, at school, born Baden' in 1880 ('Myer' household, Hazleton East Ward). On 10 Feb 1892 a licence was issued (Luzerne Orphans' Court marriage docket No. 11054) for Henry J. Meier, born in Germany 15 Nov 1866, residing in Hazleton, moulder, not previously married, and Annie A. Higgins, born New Philadelphia, PA, 2 Oct 1867, residing in Hazleton; they married 1 Mar 1892 at Hazleton (officiant read as 'Rev. Nich. Fo[rve?]' in the Meier notes and 'Rev. Nich. Gow…' in the Irish/PA notes). This docket is the first record spelling the name 'Meier' — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it. Sons Fred (1892) and Henry Jr. (1894) were born in Hazleton; Mary (1897) and Madeline (1900) in Wilkes-Barre (Ward 16, 1897–1900, FS tree); the family was in Tamaqua, Schuylkill Co. c.1903–06 (William b. c.1904; Joseph John b. 30 Jun 1906), near Anna's birthplace. In 1910 (Wilkes-Barre Ward 14, ED 158, sheet 20B, 28 Apr 1910, 14 Mill Street, dwelling 376, family 388) he was Henry J. Meier, head, 43, married 19 years, born Germany, both parents born Germany, immigrated 1868, citizenship 'Pa' (first papers only), moulder in a moulding shop, renting; Annie 42 had borne 7 children, 6 living. In 1920 (Ward 15, ED 262, sheet 6A, 7–8 Jan 1920, 298 Barney St, renting) he was 53, molder at an iron works — but this sheet gives his birthplace as 'New York' (informant error; every other record says Germany/Baden); son Henry Jr. lived next door at 296 Barney. In 1926 he was 'Henry', moulder, of Wilkes-Barre (William's application, which wrongly says born 'Penna.'). In 1940 (Ward 15, ED 40-330, sheet 3B, 3 Apr 1940, 16 Barney Street, owned, worth $3,000; same house in 1935) he was 'Meyer, Henry J., 72, born Germany, naturalized ("Na"), moulder at an iron works', with Anna A. (72), Mary C. (42) and Joseph J. (33). The citizenship change from 'Pa' (1910) to 'Na' (1940) implies his own naturalization between 1910 and 1940 (papers not found). He died, per the FamilySearch tree LTHM-1XV citing the Find a Grave index (QVG4-98K8), in Dec 1940 in Wilkes-Barre and was buried at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Township. He is NOT in the PA death index for 1939, 1940 or 1941 under Soundex M600 (Meier/Meyer/Maier/Mayer/Moore) as Henry or Harry in Luzerne (the only 1940 'Henry J Meyer' is in Erie, county 25, d. 18 Nov 1940, p.1426), nor in the NYS (ex-NYC) index 1931–71 at a fitting age; no Henry/Harry Meier in the Wilkes-Barre newspaper death lists 1929–40 and 1945. Possible explanations: a late-filed or misspelled certificate (Heinrich, Mier), or the tree's '1940' merged with Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick), 47, d. 9 Feb 1940 Wilkes-Barre. Two Long Island Henry Meier deaths (Huntington 21 Jul 1931, cert. 44888; Hempstead 24 May 1937, cert. 34005) were flagged as leads before the 1940 census proved him alive on 3 Apr 1940 — they cannot be him. A FamilySearch 'Henry Higgins (1866–1940)' (MWTJ-M9C) with identical dates is an unrelated man born in Bethnal Green, London, buried in Outremont, Quebec.

facts.label: Surname
facts.value: Surname spelling history (Mayer→Meier): Munzingen registers write Mayer 1820–1862 (1820 marriage 'Henericus Mayer', 1835 birth 'Friedrich Mayer', 1862 marriage 'Friedrich Mayer'); 1870 US census 'Meyer, Frederick'; 1880 census 'Myer, Friedrich'; the 1892 Luzerne marriage docket No. 11054 is the first record spelling it 'Meier' (Henry J. Meier) — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it; 'Meier' is consistent from 1910 on (1910, 1920, 1926, 1930, 1950 records; PA death indexes 1911/1913/1963) except 'Meyer, Henry J.' in the 1940 census; no formal name change is recorded.
